note: Content & Scene Safety Policy -- general child-safety rules distinct from phase2/data/safety/content_restrictions.json's Islamic-specific restrictions. Wired into the SAME check_content_restrictions() enforcement path (episode_consistency_check.py), not a parallel checker. Every BLOCK/REVIEW_REQUIRED here is a channel/child-safety policy decision, never a claimed Islamic ruling (those remain in content_restrictions.json with real evidence).

rules.description: Pornographic, sexualized, or sexually suggestive content of any kind, especially involving minors.
rules.notes: Zero tolerance, no context exception. Existing critical_child_safety rules elsewhere in this system already govern this absolutely; this registry entry ensures the same production-packaging gate enforces it.

rules.description: Profanity, obscenity, slurs, degrading insults, threats.
rules.notes: Context matters: an educational mention of 'bad words exist, don't use them' is different from a character actually saying one. This registry flags literal use only; discussion-about-language is not blocked. Real word list populated after adversarial testing found the placeholder was never filled in -- this list remains intentionally small/conservative (severe, unambiguous cases only) since children's-show conflict dialogue legitimately includes mild friction ('that's not fair!') that must not be blocked.

rules.description: Gore, torture, graphic injury, glorified fighting/weapons used aggressively.
rules.notes: Reuses/aligns with existing restriction_005 (violence) in content_restrictions.json -- not a duplicate ruling, a parallel enforcement surface for the same policy.

rules.description: Self-harm or suicide content involving children.
rules.notes: Absolute block, no exceptions for this channel's audience.

rules.description: Drug use, intoxicant/alcohol promotion, smoking/vaping shown positively.
rules.notes: Islamic ruling on alcohol lives in restriction_007 (content_restrictions.json, VERIFIED_ISLAMIC_RESTRICTION). This entry is the separate CHILD_SAFETY_POLICY layer -- glorification/promotion is blocked as child-safety regardless of the religious ruling.
Parallels restriction_008 (Islamic ruling) with a CHILD_SAFETY_POLICY layer -- glorification blocked regardless of religious classification.

rules.description: Theft, vandalism, or crime presented positively/rewarded.
rules.notes: A character making a mistake and facing consequence/learning is NOT this category -- see safety_012 for the distinction. KNOWN LIMITATION found via real adversarial testing: 'he stole the toy and everyone celebrated how clever he was' was NOT caught before this fix, and countless other paraphrases of the same pattern still won't be -- keyword lists cannot achieve full semantic coverage of 'theft framed as admirable' in all its phrasings. This is a genuine, permanent limitation of pattern-based detection, not a bug to be fully closed by adding more phrases. Human review remains necessary for subtler cases.

rules.description: Dangerous stunts, fire/electrical hazards, reckless behavior presented as imitable by children.
rules.notes: REVIEW not BLOCK, since e.g. 'don't play with matches' safety-lesson content legitimately mentions the hazard to teach avoiding it.

rules.description: Hatred or hostility toward a group based on religion, nationality, ethnicity, race, disability, gender, profession, or region; portraying an entire group as inherently bad.
rules.notes: Individual character flaws are fine; attributing them to an entire real-world group is not. Real phrase list populated after adversarial testing found the original aliases were literal unmatchable bracket placeholders ('all [group] are bad'), not real text -- a genuine bug, not just a coverage gap.

rules.description: Glorification of terrorism, violent extremism, attacks on civilians, incitement to violence.
rules.notes: Absolute block, no context exception for a children's channel.

rules.description: Animal cruelty depicted without clear condemnation.
rules.notes: Real, normal pet/farm/wildlife/educational animal content remains fully allowed -- see phase2/data/safety/animal_policy_registry.json for the structured per-species registry, not a blacklist.

rules.description: NOT a restriction -- a documented exception. A mistake shown, then corrected/apologized for, is ALLOW. Bullying shown briefly and clearly condemned is ALLOW_WITH_CONTEXT. Bullying celebrated/unaddressed is BLOCK (see safety_013).
rules.notes: This entry exists so the scanner has an explicit documented carve-out, not an implicit one a future editor might remove by accident.

rules.description: Bullying/cruelty shown as admirable, funny at the victim's expense with no consequence, or encouraged.
rules.notes: Distinct from safety_012's allowed depiction-for-lesson case.
